questions.question:
Given below are two statements:
Statement-I: For diamagnetic substance -1≤χ<0, where χ is the magnetic susceptibility.
Statement-II: Diamagnetic substances when placed in an external magnetic field, tend to move from stronger to weaker part of the field.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.

 

[JEE Main 2023, 10 Apr (Shift 2)]
options: Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is true.
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is false.
questions.explanation:
Magnetic susceptibility (χ\chi) measures how easily a substance becomes magnetized in an external magnetic field.

For Diamagnetic substances: These substances develop a weak induced magnetization in a direction opposite to the applied field. Therefore, χ\chi is always negative.

the range is mathematically expressed as:-1≤χ<0-1 \le \chi < 0

Diamagnetic materials exhibit a property called feeble repulsion.

When placed in a non-uniform external magnetic field, the induced magnetic poles in a diamagnetic substance are oriented such that they are repelled by the external field.

Because of this repulsion, the substance experiences a net force that pushes it away from the high-intensity regions of the magnetic field toward the lower-intensity regions.

Example: If you place a diamagnetic liquid in a watch glass between two closely spaced pole pieces of a magnet, the liquid will depress in the center (the strongest part of the field).

Let quadratic curve passing through the point \((-1,0)\) and touching the line \(y=x\) at \((1,1)\) be \(\mathrm{y}=f(x)\). Then the \(x\)-intercept of the normal to the curve at the point \((\alpha, \alpha+1)\) in the first quadrant is.........

Let the quadratic curve be \(y=f(x)=ax^2+bx+c\).

Since it passes through \((-1,0)\),

\(a-b+c=0\).

Since it touches the line \(y=x\) at \((1,1)\),

\(a+b+c=1\).

The slope of the line \(y=x\) is \(1\).

Therefore, \(f'(1)=1\).

Since \(f'(x)=2ax+b\), we get

\(2a+b=1\).

Subtracting \(a-b+c=0\) from \(a+b+c=1\),

we get \(2b=1\).

Hence, \(b=\dfrac12\).

Using \(2a+b=1\), we get

\(2a+\dfrac12=1\).

Therefore, \(a=\dfrac14\).

Using \(a+b+c=1\), we get

\(\dfrac14+\dfrac12+c=1\).

Hence, \(c=\dfrac14\).

Thus, \(f(x)=\dfrac{(x+1)^2}{4}\).

The point \((\alpha,\alpha+1)\) lies on the curve,

so \(\alpha+1=\dfrac{(\alpha+1)^2}{4}\).

Since the point is in the first quadrant, \(\alpha+1>0\).

Therefore, \(\alpha+1=4\), so \(\alpha=3\).

The point is \((3,4)\).

The slope of the tangent there is

\(f'(3)=\dfrac{3+1}{2}=2\).

Therefore, the slope of the normal is \(-\dfrac12\).

The normal is \(y-4=-\dfrac12(x-3)\).

Putting \(y=0\), we get

\(-4=-\dfrac12(x-3)\).

Hence, \(x=11\)

questions.question:
The sum of all the four-digit numbers that can be formed using all the digits \(2,1,2,3\) is equal to

 

[JEE Main 2023, 10 Apr (Shift 2)]
questions.explanation:
The digits are \(1,2,2,3\).

The total number of distinct four-digit numbers is \(\dfrac{4!}{2!}=12\).

Consider any one fixed place, such as the thousands place.

If the digit \(1\) is fixed at this place, the remaining digits \(2,2,3\) can be arranged in \(\dfrac{3!}{2!}=3\) ways.

Therefore, the digit \(1\) occurs \(3\) times at each place.

If the digit \(3\) is fixed at the same place, the remaining digits \(1,2,2\) can also be arranged in \(\dfrac{3!}{2!}=3\) ways.

Therefore, the digit \(3\) also occurs \(3\) times at each place.

The digit \(2\) occurs in the remaining \(12-3-3=6\) numbers at each place.

Thus, the sum of all digits appearing at any fixed place is \(1(3)+2(6)+3(3)=24\).

The total contribution of all four places is \(24(1000+100+10+1)\).

Therefore, the sum of all the numbers is \(24\times1111=26664\).

Hence, the required answer is \(26664\).
